![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200695/assets/28a16cda2f97557c23908fcd45928da5d4e11102343c33eaf07d1990fb0b6baf.png)

The graph of $y={f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above. Which of the following could be the graph of $y=f(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that critical points of $y=f(x)$ occur when ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ or ${f}^{′}(x)$ does not exist. In our case, there is one critical point: 

$\,$ $x=0$ 

Also, we have the following: 

- If ${f}^{′}(x)>0$ then $f(x)$ is increasing.

- If ${f}^{′}(x)<0$ then $f(x)$ is decreasing.

We can now summarize the information from the graph in the table below.

| $x$ | $(-\infty ,0)$ | $0$ | $(0,\infty )$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}^{′}$ | $+$ | $0$ | $-$ |
| $f$ | $↗$ | $\text{max}$ | $↘$ |

Let's now sketch the graph of $y=f(x):$

- First, we draw the critical point. We choose an arbitrary point on the vertical line $x=0,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200695/assets/ea6ac357860556acba25d5510ff0e65a4b66acc65e035cd218715b0e96807519.png)

- Next, we consider the behavior of $y=f(x)$ in the neighborhood of the critical points:

- Since $f(x)$ is increasing $↗$ on $(-\infty ,0)$ and decreasing $↘$ on $(0,\infty )$, the graph of $y=f(x)$ goes down to the left and to the right of $x=0.$

So, we can draw as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200695/assets/2aafc298a8a7b0856d339582bb1236e9ae97c728eba103c703998e14455fdde5.png)

 

- Finally, by connecting and extending the existing parts with a smooth curve, we obtain a possible graph of $y=f(x):$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200695/assets/04ec8de5abfecc23f3b4fb844b4e725e2a4f94aeb12bef61cda6356a6522826c.png)

**Note:** The graph we obtained is not the only possible one. Any similar graph that's shifted vertically up or down could also be considered a possible $y=f(x).$
